value: evening or nocturnal (most movement in evening or nocturnal diel periods)
method: radio-telemetry plus implanted tri-axial accelerometer data-loggers (1 Hz); random-forest classification of movement versus immobility, validated against field observations; activity budgets by diel period
conditions: Free-ranging adult male western diamond-backed rattlesnakes (males only; 12 of 19 implanted snakes analysed, the rest lost to device failures), Indio Mountains Research Station, Hudspeth County, Texas, June 2016 to August 2018 (the 19 implanted were 17 males and two females; seven units failed; median 35 days of data per snake, range 6-289). Diel periods as defined in the Table 4 footnote: morning 0601-1000 h, diurnal 1001-1800 h, evening 1801-2100 h, nocturnal 2101-0600 h. Snakes located by radio telemetry at least twice weekly; no bait or lure mentioned; the paper does not say how the snakes were captured. The timing pattern was the same in all active seasons (spring, summer non-mating, summer mating, fall), but daily movement duration varied by season and increased in the summer mating season (next abstract sentence); the Results also report 'some variation in the proportion of time spent moving within diel periods across seasons'. Devices were implanted and the paper does not measure implant effects on behaviour (it states implantation was chosen 'to minimize the effects of the device on individual behavior'). Study is validation of a logging method; the species is highly sedentary.

method: visual transect survey (600 m x 10 m, 0.6 ha) walked hourly from 08:30 to 19:30 (12 walks) on two spring days; passive counts without capture or handling
conditions: Free-living lizards at Farellones, central Chile, 4 and 5 November (austral spring), 245 recorded observations (records, not unique individuals, so the same animal may be counted more than once); no lizards were active before 09:00. Adults gave a unimodal pattern with most records between 13:00 and 14:00 (maximum 39 records); juveniles 'presented a relatively constant activity during the day' (abstract), and juveniles outnumbered adults only at 19:30, the last hour. Spring only; no other season or night sampling. No bait or lure; no capture.
